transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Janelle Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Karen Li (CISO - Horizon), Devon Brooks (Platform Eng), Soroush Patel (Data Privacy)

[00:00] Janelle: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, really quick intro — I'm Janelle from Redwood, this is Marco our solutions engineer. Can everyone say hi?
[00:08] Karen: Hi, Karen Li, CISO at Horizon.
[00:10] Devon: Devon, platform engineering.
[00:12] Soroush: Soroush, privacy.
[00:15] Marco: Thanks, quick agenda — security posture, what kind of deployment you're considering (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and then dive into specifics: SOC2/ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and data retention.

[02:05] Karen: High level — Horizon handles PHI, we have to be HIPAA aware and our security team is vetting any vendor. We're evaluating hosted and dedicated first, private deployment if we need on-prem. Main asks: SOC2 Type II or ISO 27001, SSO/SAML support with SCIM for provisioning, audit logs retained for at least 2 years, and customer-managed keys ideally.

[03:20] Janelle: Got it. We are SOC2 Type II and have ISO cert — we'll send those artifacts. For keys we support BYOK via KMS integrations, and for private deployments we can integrate with customer HSMs.

[04:00] Devon: Quick question on the hosted offering — if we use hosted can we still have customer-managed keys?
[04:12] Marco: Short answer: yes, with our hosted offering we support cross-account KMS where the customer maintains keys in their cloud KMS and we perform envelope encryption. There's also an option for dedicated pools with customer key control. For fully private (VPC/on-prem) you can bring your own HSM. Note: some of the docs call it K-M-S and sometimes we typed as KMS, apologies for audio.

[05:00] Karen: And audit logs — we need immutable logs with admin actions, model access, and tokenization events. Retention and exportability are critical.

[05:12] Marco: We capture extensive audit logs — admin actions, model version rollouts, API calls, token usage and errors. Logs can be forwarded to your SIEM via syslog/CloudWatch/Stackdriver, or we can provide a secure download with signed manifests. Retention configurable per account; default retention for hosted is 90 days but we can extend it for enterprise plans or Dedicated/Private deployments.

[07:35] Soroush: Do logs include prompt/response content? That's sensitive. We can't send PHI to third parties in clear text.

[07:45] Janelle: By default we redact PII in logs and content logging is opt-in. For enterprise customers, logs can be configured to exclude full prompt/response or to encrypt logs with customer-managed keys so only you can decrypt. For private deployments, no logs leave your environment unless you configure them to.

[09:10] Karen: For SSO we use SAML with Okta and use SCIM for provisioning — we need provisioning and deprovisioning to be fast for contractors. Is SAML supported?

[09:22] Marco: Yes, we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM 2.0. We also offer SAML session lifetime config and role mapping to RBAC. Quick note: sometimes internal docs auto-generate 'Sammel' or 'Samal' in transcripts so watch for typos — we'll send the SSO guide.

[11:00] Devon: About RBAC — we need fine-grained roles: team-level model access, ability to restrict certain model families for PHI, and audit-level access for compliance folks.

[11:12] Marco: Our RBAC supports role-based roles and attribute-based access; you can map SAML groups to roles and have least-privileged model access. For dedicated/private we support tenant isolation and token-level scoping so engineers only see what they should.

[13:30] Karen: Encryption in transit and at rest — what algorithms and KMS providers do you support? Also, any HSM certifications?

[13:44] Marco: TLS 1.2/1.3 for transit, AES-256 for at-rest envelope encryption. We integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure KeyVault; for HSMs we support customer HSMs via PKCS#11 and can work with AWS CloudHSM. HSM certifications are dependent on the provider; for Redwood Private we can integrate with FIPS 140-2 HSMs.

[15:05] Karen: Do you provide attestation that keys are not available to Redwood staff for hosted?

[15:12] Janelle: Yes — with customer-managed KMS, Redwood does not have access to the plaintext keys; we operate on encrypted blobs. We'll include language in the security whitepaper and contract addendum.

[17:00] Devon: What about model KV cache and prefix caching — can that leak data?

[17:12] Marco: We do continuous batching and KV cache optimizations. For enterprise customers we have cache scoping and configurable TTLs and can disable certain caches. I know docs sometimes say 'KV cash' in older notes — it's KV cache. For PHI use-cases we recommend dedicated pools or private deployment to avoid multi-tenant cache risks.

[19:10] Soroush: Regulatory question — data residency. We need processing to remain in US regions only.

[19:20] Janelle: We support regional hosting and can pin requests to US-only regions. Dedicated and private give you more control; hosted can be region-restricted for enterprise contracts.

[21:00] Karen: Pen testing and vuln disclosures — do you run a regular pen test, have bug bounty?

[21:10] Marco: We run annual pen tests and have a coordinated vulnerability disclosure program. We can share redacted reports. We'll include the latest pen test summary and our vulnerability policy.

[23:45] Devon: On logs again — we want signed immutable logs to meet audit requirements. Is that possible?

[23:55] Marco: Yes, we can generate signed manifests and provide log integrity proofs. Also you can ship logs to your SIEM where you control retention and immutability settings.

[26:30] Karen: What's the recommended path if we start with hosted and later move to dedicated or private? Does that cause downtime or data migration headaches?

[26:45] Janelle: We support smooth rollouts and model pinning. For customer data, we can export accounts and keys; moving to Dedicated involves provisioning capacity and updating routing policies. There may be a short cutover window for keys but we plan for zero-downtime migrations where possible; Marco can walk through specifics in the technical deep dive.

[30:05] Soroush: Contractual language — we need specific clauses around data processing, subprocessing, and incident notification timelines.

[30:18] Janelle: Understood. We have a DPA template and incident response SLAs; we'll send templates and legal contacts.

[32:00] Karen: One more — can we do a short benchmark to validate latency for our workflows? We need 95th percentile under 300ms for small chat-ish sequences.

[32:12] Marco: Yes, we can run a focused benchmark on Hosted with your sample prompts; for tighter SLAs Dedicated or colocated Private gives better predictability. We'll run a perf test and share raw logs.

[35:50] Devon: Operational question — how do we rotate keys and what is the impact on ongoing sessions?

[36:00] Marco: Key rotation is supported via a gradual key swap process — we rotate envelope keys and rewrap metadata; sessions should remain intact. For HSM-backed rotation there are standard steps; we'll document the runbook.

[38:30] Karen: Anything on forensic access? In an incident, can you provide logs and traces quickly?

[38:40] Janelle: Yes, we have on-call for security and can provide expedited log exports and traces; chain-of-custody processes are in our incident runbook.

[41:10] Soroush: Are there any limits on how long we can retain logs in hosted if we ask for 2 years?

[41:20] Marco: Hosted default is 90 days, but enterprise plans or Dedicated allow extended retention; for 2 years we'd likely use log archival to your S3 or a customer-managed store — that'll be part of the enterprise add-on.

[44:00] Karen: For proof-of-concept, we want a small pilot using non-PHI data first, but during the pilot we'd like to see audit logs and KMS integration.

[44:12] Janelle: Totally reasonable — pilot with non-PHI, we'll enable audit logging and a sandbox KMS integration so you can validate configs.

[46:30] Marco: Quick caveat — sometimes the transcript generator messes up product names; our Dedicated product used to be called Redwood Dedicated, private is Redwood Private, and the console is Redwood Console.

[48:00] Karen: Ok, recap?

[48:05] Janelle: Recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO attestations and pen test summary, share SSO/SCIM guide, VPC/KMS integration docs, sample audit logs, and DPA templates. Marco will prepare a technical deep dive for infra and run a benchmark with your sample prompts. Karen to share data retention policy and regulatory constraints. We'll find time for a deep dive week of 2025-12-01.

[49:10] Karen: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.

[49:20] Devon: Thanks.

[49:25] Soroush: Thanks all.

[49:30] Janelle: Thanks, we'll follow up by email with artifacts.

[50:00] <call ends>
